definitions_and_conventions: L2 consists of random variables with finite second Lp norm and is a Hilbert space [PDF pp.1-2 / printed pp.5-6, Section 1.1; anchors: the Lp definition and the p=2 paragraph].
The L2 inner product is <X,Y>_L2 = E(XY) [PDF p.2 / printed p.6, equation (1.1); anchor: the first displayed equality].
The centered versions of X and Y are X-EX and Y-EY, respectively [PDF p.2 / printed p.6, equation (1.2); anchor: both centered factors].
Covariance is the signed scalar E[(X-EX)(Y-EY)], exactly the inner product of those centered vectors [PDF p.2 / printed p.6, equation (1.2); anchor: both displayed equalities].

The book convention makes nonlinear expressions bind before expectation, so the covariance display means expectation of the product of the two parenthesized centered factors [PDF p.1 / printed p.5, footnote 2, and PDF p.2 / printed p.6, equation (1.2); anchors: the expectation-notation convention and the covariance display].

No independence, identical-distribution, or centering-as-an-input assumption is imposed; centering is performed by subtracting each expectation [PDF p.2 / printed p.6, equation (1.2) and Remark 1.1.1; anchors: the displayed centered vectors and absence of additional premises in the remark].

contract_plain_english: For square-integrable real random variables on a fixed probability space, covariance is exactly the L2 inner product of the centered variables X-EX and Y-EY. Remark 1.1.1 uses this equality to give a qualitative picture: greater same-direction alignment corresponds to a larger signed inner product and hence larger signed covariance. It does not state a normalized correlation formula, an absolute-value claim, or any quantitative Cauchy-Schwarz covariance bound; that inequality appears separately in the following section [PDF pp.1-2 / printed pp.5-6, Section 1.1 equations (1.1)-(1.2), Remark 1.1.1, and the later Section 1.2 Cauchy-Schwarz paragraph; structural anchors: the covariance identity, the complete remark, and the section boundary].
